spec.description: Seconds since the last harbor-cache-recovery cron job completed; the schedule is every 5 min. Yellow at 30 min, red at 60 min. 30 min is 6x the schedule and is the same line the `HarborCacheRecoveryStale` alert uses, so the tile reacts to sustained absence of the job rather than to one late or failed run - individual run failures are normal here and are covered by the per-run alerts in the same rule group. Both lines are calibrated to the 5-minute schedule, which is the per-cluster `harbor_cache_recovery.schedule` key - a cluster moved off `*/5` needs them moved with it. `NO COMPLETED JOB` = no successful run is retained, and it reads red because the tile cannot tell a healthy cluster from a dead CronJob: the CronJob keeps 3 successful Jobs and sets no `ttlSecondsAfterFinished`, and a TTL under ~360 s, a history limit of 0, a renamed job or a cluster whose first run has not landed would each empty it.

spec.expr: max by (cluster)(time() - gha_capacity_reconcile_last_success_timestamp_seconds{cluster=~"$cluster"})

spec.description: Seconds since the *worst* ARC capacity-monitor listener last completed a reconcile loop - the max across listeners, so one wedged listener is visible. Yellow at 15 min, red at 30 min. The floor is the 180 s scrape interval of the monitoring/arc-listeners job, so the tile idles near 200 s. A listener whose pod dies has its series dropped after Prometheus's 5 min staleness horizon, which caps pod churn near 480 s; a listener that stays up with a wedged loop climbs without bound, and that is the case this tile exists to catch. It remains structurally quiet: the 90-day maximum is 592 s, so it has never been yellow, and total loss of every listener pod blanks the tile rather than reddening it - panel-115 and the `ARCListenerStall` alert cover that case. If stale, capacity dashboards and `ARCListenerStall` go blind.

spec.description: Max conntrack table utilization across all nodes. Yellow at >=10%, red at >=25%. These are engineering judgement, not an observed failure: no saturation event exists anywhere in 90 days of fleet data - the 14-day fleet peak is 4.54% and none of ~237k node lifetimes ever exceeded 5%. Read the value as an anomaly indicator rather than a saturation gauge, because the ratio is dominated by `nf_conntrack_max` heterogeneity rather than by connection load: the worst-reading node is not the busiest node. The 4.54% peak was 23,782 entries on a 524,288-limit node, while the fleet's busiest node at 39,669 entries read only 2.52% behind a 1,572,864 limit. Saturation drops new connections (IPv6 SNAT side effect).

spec.description: Per-cluster count of broken workloads, not replicas, and only workloads that have a tile in the row below: this tile is an index into that row, so its value is how many of those tiles are non-green rather than how much is broken in the cluster. Coverage is an explicit allowlist of namespaces and workload names, not a filter on what is broken, so anything outside it - an orphaned Deployment, a namespace nobody tiles, a DaemonSet added without a tile - reads zero here no matter how broken it is. The allowlist mirrors each tile's own selector: harbor-system entire, because the Harbor tile is namespace-wide, for both the Deployment and the StatefulSet term; the named Deployment of every other per-service tile; and the DaemonSets the twelve stuck-pod severity tiles name, with the five hf-cache-mount tiers counted as the single unit their shared tile measures. NodeLocal DNS and DCGM run as DaemonSets but are indexed by Liveness instead, which applies the scrape-target ratio their tiles use rather than an unavailability budget. A Deployment counts when it has no available replicas or a rollout Kubernetes has abandoned (Progressing=false), a StatefulSet when it has no ready replicas, a DaemonSet when either it exceeds a budget of clamp_min(0.5% of desired, 1.5) pods in excess of the cluster's NotReady node count for a sustained hour, or at least three quarters of it is unavailable for a sustained fifteen minutes. The fraction reading subtracts no NotReady count, so node churn cannot hide a total outage from it the way it can from the budget reading. Both are the lines the stuck-pod severity tiles turn yellow on, so a DaemonSet cannot be counted here while its own tile is still green. An autoscaling Deployment stays available while it scales, so BuildKit scale-up never registers. Two further terms count kube-state-metrics being down or emitting no Deployment metrics. Green=0, red>=1: every unit is one non-green tile below. An empty result renders red. If a cluster loses its metrics pipeline entirely its tile disappears instead - that case needs an absent_over_time alert rule, not this panel.
spec.title: Workloads [cluster]

spec.expr: (count by (cluster) ((100 - 100 * avg by (cluster, job) (up{cluster=~"$cluster", job=~"monitoring/coredns|monitoring/nodelocaldns|monitoring/arc-listeners|dcgm-exporter"})) >= 5) or (group by (cluster)(up{cluster=~"$cluster"}) * 0)) + (count by (cluster) ((100 - 100 * avg by (cluster, job) (up{cluster=~"$cluster", job=~"monitoring/coredns|monitoring/nodelocaldns|monitoring/arc-listeners|dcgm-exporter"})) >= 10) or (group by (cluster)(up{cluster=~"$cluster"}) * 0)) + (count by (cluster) (harbor_health{cluster=~"$cluster"} == 0) or (group by (cluster)(up{cluster=~"$cluster"}) * 0)) + (count by (cluster) (group by (cluster, proxy)(haproxy_server_status{cluster=~"$cluster", proxy=~"bk_.*"}) unless group by (cluster, proxy)(haproxy_server_status{cluster=~"$cluster", proxy=~"bk_.*", state="UP"} == 1)) or (group by (cluster)(up{cluster=~"$cluster"}) * 0)) + (count by (cluster) ((100 * sum by (cluster)(rate(apiserver_request_total{cluster=~"$cluster", code=~"5.."}[5m])) / clamp_min(sum by (cluster)(rate(apiserver_request_total{cluster=~"$cluster"}[5m])), 1)) >= 0.05) or (group by (cluster)(up{cluster=~"$cluster"}) * 0)) + (count by (cluster) ((100 * max by (cluster)(node_nf_conntrack_entries{cluster=~"$cluster"} / node_nf_conntrack_entries_limit{cluster=~"$cluster"})) >= 10) or (group by (cluster)(up{cluster=~"$cluster"}) * 0)) + clamp_min(1 - ((count by (cluster)(up{cluster=~"$cluster", job=~"monitoring/coredns|monitoring/nodelocaldns|monitoring/arc-listeners|dcgm-exporter"})) or (group by (cluster)(up{cluster=~"$cluster"}) * 0)), 0)

spec.description: Per-cluster count of degraded services, normalised per service. Each scrape job (CoreDNS, NodeLocal DNS, ARC Listeners, DCGM) counts once when more than 5% of its own targets are down and twice when more than 10% are - the same 95%/90% lines all four matching per-service tiles use - so node churn on a large fleet does not register and a total outage of a small one does. Also counts Harbor unhealthy, BuildKit LB backends down, API Server 5xx>=0.05%, conntrack>=10%. A final term counts 1 when none of those four scrape jobs report at all, so a cluster whose monitoring targets deregister says so instead of reading zero degraded services. kube-state-metrics is deliberately not guarded here: no term on this tile reads it, so a KSM outage neither degrades nor blinds anything this tile measures - Workloads, Freshness and OOM/Restarts carry that guard. Green=0, yellow=1, red>=2. An empty result renders red.
spec.title: Liveness [cluster]

spec.expr: (count by (cluster) ((time() - max by (cluster)(kube_job_status_completion_time{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace="harbor-system", job_name=~"harbor-cache-recovery-.*"})) >= 1800) or (group by (cluster)(up{cluster=~"$cluster"}) * 0)) + (count by (cluster) (max by (cluster)(time() - gha_capacity_reconcile_last_success_timestamp_seconds{cluster=~"$cluster"}) >= 900) or (group by (cluster)(up{cluster=~"$cluster"}) * 0)) + (count by (cluster) ((time() - max by (cluster)(kube_job_status_completion_time{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace="arc-runners", job_name=~"zombie-cleanup-.*"})) >= 4500) or (group by (cluster)(up{cluster=~"$cluster"}) * 0)) + (count by (cluster) (sum by (cluster)(rate(node_compactor_reconcile_cycles_total{cluster=~"$cluster", status="success"}[5m])) == 0) or (group by (cluster)(up{cluster=~"$cluster"}) * 0)) + (count by (cluster)(up{cluster=~"$cluster", job="kube-state-metrics"} == 0) or (group by (cluster)(up{cluster=~"$cluster"}) * 0)) + clamp_min(1 - ((count by (cluster)(kube_job_status_completion_time{cluster=~"$cluster"})) or (group by (cluster)(up{cluster=~"$cluster"}) * 0)), 0)

spec.description: Per-cluster count of stale scheduled jobs and reconcile loops: Harbor Cache Recovery (>30m), ARC Capacity reconcile (>15m), Zombie Cleanup (>75m, i.e. one missed hourly run), Node Compactor (no successful cycle in 5m). The ARC Capacity term measures the stalest listener rather than the freshest, so a single wedged reconcile loop is visible among 45-114 emitters. Two further terms count kube-state-metrics being down or emitting no Job metrics, because the Harbor and Zombie Cleanup terms read its data and would otherwise report green about jobs they can no longer see - so a non-green tile can mean "we cannot tell" rather than "a job is late". Green=0, yellow=1, red>=2. An empty result renders red.
spec.title: Freshness [cluster]

spec.expr: (clamp_max(count by (cluster) (kube_pod_container_status_last_terminated_reason{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace="hf-cache", container="rclone", reason="OOMKilled"} unless kube_pod_container_status_last_terminated_reason{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace="hf-cache", container="rclone", reason="OOMKilled"} offset 1h), 1) or (group by (cluster)(up{cluster=~"$cluster"}) * 0)) + (count by (cluster) (max by (cluster)(increase(kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total{cluster=~"$cluster"}[1h])) >= 10) or (group by (cluster)(up{cluster=~"$cluster"}) * 0)) + (count by (cluster)(up{cluster=~"$cluster", job="kube-state-metrics"} == 0) or (group by (cluster)(up{cluster=~"$cluster"}) * 0)) + clamp_min(1 - ((count by (cluster)(kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total{cluster=~"$cluster"})) or (group by (cluster)(up{cluster=~"$cluster"}) * 0)), 0)

spec.description: Per-cluster count of diverging restart/OOM signals, each contributing 0 or 1: an hf-cache rclone container OOM-killed within the last hour, and any single container at >=10 restarts in the last hour. The OOM gauge is sticky - it stays set until the pod is replaced - so it is differenced against itself an hour ago to report OOMs in the window rather than pods carrying a stale flag. The restart term measures depth, not breadth: 20 containers restarting once reads 0, one container restarting 20 times reads 1. Two further terms count kube-state-metrics being down or emitting no restart metrics, because both other terms read its data and would otherwise report green about containers they can no longer see - so a non-green tile can mean "we cannot tell" rather than "something restarted". Green=0, yellow=1, red>=2. Restart coverage is limited to the namespaces where the restart counter is retained (see the Container Restarts tile); hf-cache is not deployed on the lf clusters, where the OOM term reads 0. An empty result renders red.
spec.title: OOM / Restarts [cluster]

options.content: Matrix of diverging-signal counts by check-type (each row) and cluster (each tile). 0 = healthy; a higher number / red = something to investigate — expand that cluster's section below for detail.
